newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--There was lacklustre attendance at yesterday's rally outside Parliament against the government's economic policies but unionists say their planned January round of protests will be more dynamic. Seamen and dockers however appeared more determined not to lose their tax perks, calling another 48-hour strike that means ports will have been shut a week by Friday morning. Secondary school teachers also announced rolling five-day strikes.
--The external payments balance has taken on alarming dimensions with fears being expressed that the deficit will reach four billion drachmas by the end of the year.

--The need for progress on the Cyprus issue to avert a clash between Greece and Turkey was underlined by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind yesterday. Rifkind will meet with Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos in London today on the British initiative.
--Cyprus, Greek-Turkish relations and the outcome of the Dublin EU summit were the focus of discussions between the foreign minister and Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday.
--Protesting farmers have Athens within their sights tomorrow, docks will be shut till the end of the week and airports hit by labour action on Friday. The noose tightens.
--The second part of the MRB poll shows Greeks aware of the advantages of convergence but pessimistic about achieving it by the year 2000.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis stands firm on the condition that there can be no dialogue with farmers as long as road blocks remain.
--Rifkind says Cyprus is a tinderbox for a possible Greek-Turkish conflict, saying it was in the interests of Europe to see progress on Cyprus.

--Journalist Elly Stai faces criminal prosecution for refusing to answer questions by a parliament fact-finding committee on the Athens casino at Floisvos, a contract which was withdrawn after being placed with a consortium.

--The development ministry hopes to keep increases on insurance premiums to 7-8 percent but private insurance companies are asking for more. Car owners may face hikes to cover the deficit in the insurance auxiliary fund.

--Ruling PASOK may be levying more and more taxes but some 83,000 people have been hired to the public service since 1993, with 4,559 entering during Simitis's tenure, and the majority of them in the pre-election period. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
